The lunar part of that script is a quick geocentric Danjon-style shadow model (enlargement factor 1.01, as in Espenak & Meeus), not the bench's lunar module: instrument check I4 has not been run. Its umbral magnitudes may be off by a few hundredths, and its times carry the Delta-T uncertainty.

would_have_written_differently_had_I_kno: Overall: under 'every primary clue must pass', the accepted date would be rejected in R-PTOL-BAB (E2 and E3 magnitudes), R-PTOL-ALEX (H3 time), R-PTOL-CHAIN (which inherits both) and R-PYDNA (season and Moon altitude). The text-only rules give accurate records tolerances that are too tight (Babylonian digits, Ptolemy's computed hours), and the narrative sources contain plain errors (Livy's 'after the solstice', Plutarch's 'μετέωρος'). I did NOT change the clue file. The bench should read these as real failure modes of ancient sky reports and score controls with a tolerance for k failed clues, or across the fork garden, rather than all-must-pass.

PB-E2-MAG and PB-E3-MAG: knowing the answer I would have set the Babylonian magnitude tolerance at about +/-2 digits (+/-0.17) and read 'more than half' as > 0.4. That would be fitting to the answer, so I record it instead of making it.
PA-H3-TIME: I would have made +/-1 h primary for Ptolemy's computed mid-times, since his reductions are off by up to about 0.6 h on these dates.

P-SEASON and P-ALT (Pydna): I would still write them as the words say. The texts are wrong about the date by about five days and about the Moon's height. Knowing this, I would have added an explicit 'season +/- 10 days' option, so that the bench can show how much a small textual error costs.

CHOICES POSSIBLY STEERED BY EXPOSURE (see docs/controls-real-drafting.md section 1). Before drafting I had seen three of these answers. In each case the result depends on the option chosen, and the primary I chose passes: (1) T1-DARK primary X4 (>= 0.60) rather than X3; I had seen 'Thuc. 2.28 0.877' in DESIGN 4.1 I2b, and X3 fails. (2) D-ECL primary X3 rather than 'total'; I had seen 'Diod. 20.5 0.995', and 'total' fails at Syracuse. (3) the +/-1 h 'ferme' tolerance in L4-DARK; I had seen '06:16 LMT' in critique issue 2, and without the tolerance L4 fails. I believe each choice follows the stated policy, but the bench owner should have them re-drafted by an unexposed agent, or report both options.

Choices that went against the answer I had seen: P-SEASON (I knew the Julian date was 21 June and wrote 'after the solstice' as primary, which fails) and the Babylonian magnitude tolerances (no exposure). This is weak evidence that the rules, not the answers, drove the drafting.

Nothing in the site, interval or calendar clues would change: every textual interval (Ptolemy's day counts, Thucydides' war-years, Xenophon's headings) holds exactly or inside its tolerance for the accepted dates, and Plutarch's Boedromion is right at offset 0.
